question: Consider $\vec{p}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{q}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$. Compare their magnitudes and directions. Hence determine whether magnitude alone is sufficient to specify a vector.
explanation:
Step 1: Magnitude of the first vector
\(|\vec{p}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+2^2}=\sqrt{9}=3\)
Step 2: Magnitude of the second vector
\(|\vec{q}|=\sqrt{(-2)^2+1^2+(-2)^2}=\sqrt{9}=3\)
Step 3: Directional relationship
Every component of $\vec{q}$ is the negative of the corresponding component of $\vec{p}$. Thus, $\vec{q}=-\vec{p}$, so the vectors point in opposite directions.
Step 4: Interpretation
Although both vectors have magnitude $3$, they are not the same vector because their directions differ.
Final Answer
The vectors have equal magnitudes and opposite directions. Therefore, magnitude alone is not sufficient to specify a vector.

options.A: $|\vec{p}|=|\vec{q}|=3$ and the vectors have the same direction; therefore magnitude alone specifies a vector.
options.B: $|\vec{p}|=3$ and $|\vec{q}|=-3$; hence magnitude alone is sufficient to specify a vector.
options.C: $|\vec{p}|=|\vec{q}|=3$ and $\vec{q}=-\vec{p}$, so they have opposite directions; therefore magnitude alone is not sufficient to specify a vector.
options.D: $|\vec{p}|=|\vec{q}|=\sqrt{5}$ and the vectors are perpendicular; therefore magnitude alone specifies a vector.
